title: Search and Glob

body.text: Two ways to search a project:
Grep searches file contents (regex supported) · Glob finds filenames by pattern
— Claude always uses these to find the relevant code before editing, so it doesn't miss a spot that needs changing.

example: "'Find every file that calls getUserData' → Grep searches for 'getUserData' across the project, finds 7 files"

title: Search before editing — a habit for big work

body.text: Claude finds all the affected spots before it starts editing
— you can help by stating the scope, like 'only in src/' or 'excluding the old test files'.

example: "'Rename the function formatPrice to formatCurrency everywhere it's used, only in src/'"

question: How are Grep and Glob different?

options.text: Grep searches file contents, Glob finds filenames
Glob deletes files, Grep creates files

question: Why is searching before editing important for refactoring?

options.text: It finds all affected spots so nothing that needs changing is missed

question: How can you make the search more accurate?

options.text: State the scope, like which folder only

question: Before editing code in big work, what habit should you have?

options.text: Search (Search/Glob) to understand the code before editing

question: What are Search and Glob for?

options.text: Searching text and files in the project
